changes: Added material-bound review_host_availability_probe evidence for codex/claude/agy, made non-human degraded review fallback require fresh host scarcity proof, rejected single-host/temporary-host fallback when two or more canonical hosts are available, kept explicit-human-approval lower assurance, updated assurance floor parsing and smoke coverage.
usage: Run node packages/main/dist/cli.js review_host_availability_probe --storyId=<story> --json, then use review_escalation_fallback_set only when the fresh probe proves host scarcity or when explicit-human-approval is supplied.
expectedOutcome: On a machine with multiple canonical hosts available, degraded single-host-environment fallback is refused and the operator is told to use full 3x2 or explicit-human-approval.
actualTranscript: Fresh probe B-7438:RHP-mrdh19fw found codex, claude, and agy available (3/3). A subsequent single-host-environment fallback attempt exited 1 with: fresh host availability probe B-7438:RHP-mrdh19fw found 3/3 canonical hosts available; use full 3x2 or explicit-human-approval.
outcomeDiff: No difference: actual behavior matched the expected refusal and cited the fresh probe ID plus host count.
limitations: No release push performed. Codex auth profiles A/B were present but real codex exec calls failed with token_invalidated/refresh_token_invalidated, so final external reviewer/quorum work used Claude CLI plus agy CLI.
pitfalls: Initial implementation missed temporary-host-unavailability coverage and two existing root-chain smokes; both were fixed. Later retired vocabulary guard required a narrow quarantine update. Codex account pool looked logged in but failed real execution, so do not trust login status alone.
